explanation: Sort names by first name and then last name so equal first names are adjacent. Compact one representative per first-name group and shrink the list. The wrapper extracts/compares first names; the callable mutates records and returns no list.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) comparisons, each potentially linear in the compared name lengths; compaction is O(n). Hash variants process each name once; sort variants sort records then compact once. Name hashing/comparison also reads characters.
spaceComplexity: C++ uses O(log n) sorting stack; Java/Python sorting may use O(n) temporary references, and Python also slices the suffix during compaction. The set holds u first names; native sorting and compaction workspace follow their library/container behavior.

correctness: After sorting, all records with one first name form a single contiguous group. Keeping only the first record of each group preserves exactly the distinct first names. The retained last name is irrelevant to the judged result.
walkthrough: Sorting [(Mira,Stone),(Noel,West),(Mira,Lake)] yields [(Mira,Lake),(Mira,Stone),(Noel,West)]. Keep Mira,Lake; skip the second Mira; keep Noel,West. The mutated record list is observed by the wrapper as [Mira,Noel].
edgeCases: Distinct last names do not make equal first names distinct.
The callable mutates the record list; the wrapper compares only distinct first names.
